title: Preacher Curl
summary: Curl with the upper arms on a preacher pad: biceps 1. The pad fixes the arm in front of the body, so the curl is hardest near the bottom. In the app it is logged as a machine exercise; use an EZ bar, dumbbells or a preacher machine.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: preacher bench or curl pad; EZ curl bar or dumbbells.

muscles.why: The elbow flexors bend the elbow; with the arm in front, the biceps is shorter at the shoulder than in an incline curl. The brachialis and brachioradialis do a large share here.

setup.text: Seat height so the armpits sit at the top of the pad.
Upper arms flat on the pad.
EZ bar, dumbbells, or the machine handles.

form_cues.cue: Lower until arms are nearly straight
form_cues.why: Lowering until the arm is nearly straight.

form_cues.cue: Curl up without lifting your elbows
form_cues.why: Upper arms stay on the pad.

form_cues.cue: Stop just before the forearms go vertical
Control the bottom of each rep. Don't drop into it.
form_cues.why: Training the long-length (arm nearly straight) half of the preacher curl grew the biceps more than the short-length half.

form_cues.cue: Don't lift the elbows off the pad
form_cues.why: It takes tension off at the top.

bias_tweaks.change: Bias the bottom half at the end of a set
bias_tweaks.effect: Long-length partials grew the elbow flexors more than short-length partials.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Full range stays the default; full and lengthened partials gave similar growth in another study.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Dropping fast into the bottom of the rep.
mistakes.fix: Lower under control; stop just short of locking out hard.
Armpits at the top of the pad.

misconceptions.myth: Preacher curls are best for the biceps.
misconceptions.reality: In a 2026 MRI study, incline curls grew the biceps more than preacher curls.

misconceptions.myth: Cables beat bars on the preacher bench.
misconceptions.reality: Cable and barbell preacher curls gave similar growth.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Low-risk to push close to failure; control the bottom on the last reps.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Arm behind the body; grew the biceps more than preacher curls.
Cable curl facing away; long-length biceps work.

notes: Equipment note: the app logs this as a machine exercise (equipment 'machine'); its equipment needs are a preacher bench plus an EZ bar or dumbbells, and every version is logged the same way.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
